constraints: Leg press and all knee work — never bend the knee past 90°
Sharp, sudden, or worsening pain means stop that set
Machine-based — the machines guide the movement and keep it safe
At least one full rest day between gym sessions
Start lighter than you think — only the last two reps should feel hard
goals: Strong quads to support and protect both knees
Be in the best possible shape going into surgery, if it's needed

weeks.label: Week 1 — Back at it, a step up
weeks.note: You finished the first program brilliantly — this block steps everything up a notch. The upper-body moves go to 3 sets, and there's a new backwards treadmill walk that's great for your knees. Same rules as always: start light, the last two reps are the only hard ones, and never past 90° on the leg press.

days.name: Full Body — Machines · Session 1
warmup: Recumbent bike, 8–10 minutes at Level 2–3 resistance
Comfortable, conversational pace — just enough to warm the knees and get the blood moving

exercises.name: Leg Press (Machine)
exercises.load: Last 2 reps should feel hard — add a little weight when 12 feels easy
exercises.cue: Feet shoulder-width, toes slightly out. Lower only until the knees reach 90° — no deeper. Push through the whole foot. Don't lock the knees hard at the top.
exercises.alternative: Keep the same weight and slow it right down — 3 seconds down, 3 seconds up.
exercises.stopIf: Sharp, sudden, or worsening knee pain — stop the set. Never let the knees bend past 90°.

exercises.name: Leg Extension (Seated Machine)
exercises.load: Light — precision over weight, hold 2s at the top
exercises.cue: Straighten fully at the top, hold, then lower slowly over 3 counts. Keep your hips back in the seat. This is precision work — the weight stays light.
exercises.alternative: Do only the top half of the movement if the full range is uncomfortable.
exercises.stopIf: Any sharp pain around the kneecap — drop the weight or stop.

exercises.name: Seated Leg Curl (Machine)
exercises.cue: Full range both ways. Control the weight back in — don't let it snap. Keep your hips pressed into the seat.
exercises.alternative: Lighten the weight and focus on a slow, controlled return.
exercises.stopIf: Cramp or sharp pain behind the knee — ease off and stretch gently.

exercises.name: Seated Calf Raise (Machine)
exercises.cue: Pause and squeeze at the top, pause and stretch at the bottom. No bouncing.
exercises.alternative: Fewer reps with a longer squeeze at the top.
exercises.stopIf: Sharp calf pain — stop and stretch gently.

exercises.name: Chest Press (Seated Machine)
exercises.cue: Sit tall. Push smoothly — no thrusting or jerking. Full reach without locking the elbows. Slow on the way back, 2 counts.
exercises.alternative: One arm at a time if the machine allows, or reduce the weight.
exercises.stopIf: Shoulder pinching — lower the weight or shorten the range.

exercises.name: Lat Pulldown (Machine)
exercises.cue: Wide grip. Pull the bar to your upper chest and lean back only slightly. Squeeze the lats at the bottom, control the way up.
exercises.alternative: Use a lighter weight and a narrower, more comfortable grip.
exercises.stopIf: Shoulder or elbow pain — go lighter.

exercises.name: Seated Row (Machine / Cable)
exercises.cue: Sit tall, chest up. Pull your elbows back and squeeze your shoulder blades together. Don't round your back or swing.
exercises.alternative: Lighten the weight and pause for a second at the squeeze.
exercises.stopIf: Lower-back pain — reduce the weight and keep your chest tall.

exercises.name: Backwards Treadmill Walk
exercises.cue: Hold the rails, take small steps, and look ahead — not down. Walking backwards uphill is brilliant for the muscles that protect the knee.
exercises.alternative: New to it? Start at 5 minutes and add a minute each session until you reach the full 10.
exercises.stopIf: Any loss of balance or knee pain — slow the belt down or step off onto the side rails.

cooldown: Recumbent bike, 3–4 minutes very easy at Level 1
Seated quad stretch — 30 seconds each leg, gentle pull only, no pain
Seated calf stretch with a towel — 30 seconds each leg
Seated hamstring stretch — 30 seconds each leg, stop at the first gentle pull

Comfortable, conversational pace — just enough to warm the knees and get the blood moving

exercises.name: Leg Press (Machine)
exercises.cue: Feet shoulder-width, toes slightly out. Lower only until the knees reach 90° — no deeper. Push through the whole foot. Don't lock the knees hard at the top.
exercises.alternative: Keep the same weight and slow it right down — 3 seconds down, 3 seconds up.
exercises.stopIf: Sharp, sudden, or worsening knee pain — stop the set. Never let the knees bend past 90°.

exercises.name: Leg Extension (Seated Machine)
exercises.load: Hold 3 seconds at the top this week
exercises.cue: Straighten fully at the top, hold, then lower slowly over 3 counts. Keep your hips back in the seat. This is precision work — the weight stays light.
exercises.alternative: Do only the top half of the movement if the full range is uncomfortable.
exercises.stopIf: Any sharp pain around the kneecap — drop the weight or stop.

exercises.name: Seated Leg Curl (Machine)
exercises.load: Nudge the weight up if 14 was easy
exercises.cue: Full range both ways. Control the weight back in — don't let it snap. Keep your hips pressed into the seat.
exercises.alternative: Lighten the weight and focus on a slow, controlled return.
exercises.stopIf: Cramp or sharp pain behind the knee — ease off and stretch gently.

exercises.name: Seated Calf Raise (Machine)
exercises.cue: Pause and squeeze at the top, pause and stretch at the bottom. No bouncing.
exercises.alternative: Fewer reps with a longer squeeze at the top.
exercises.stopIf: Sharp calf pain — stop and stretch gently.

exercises.name: Chest Press (Seated Machine)
exercises.load: Nudge the weight up if 12 is easy
exercises.cue: Sit tall. Push smoothly — no thrusting or jerking. Full reach without locking the elbows. Slow on the way back, 2 counts.
exercises.alternative: One arm at a time if the machine allows, or reduce the weight.
exercises.stopIf: Shoulder pinching — lower the weight or shorten the range.

exercises.name: Lat Pulldown (Machine)
exercises.load: Nudge the weight up if 12 is easy
exercises.cue: Wide grip. Pull the bar to your upper chest and lean back only slightly. Squeeze the lats at the bottom, control the way up.
exercises.alternative: Use a lighter weight and a narrower, more comfortable grip.
exercises.stopIf: Shoulder or elbow pain — go lighter.

exercises.name: Seated Row (Machine / Cable)
exercises.load: Nudge the weight up if 12 is easy
exercises.cue: Sit tall, chest up. Pull your elbows back and squeeze your shoulder blades together. Don't round your back or swing.
exercises.alternative: Lighten the weight and pause for a second at the squeeze.
exercises.stopIf: Lower-back pain — reduce the weight and keep your chest tall.

exercises.name: Backwards Treadmill Walk
exercises.cue: Hold the rails, take small steps, and look ahead — not down. Walking backwards uphill is brilliant for the muscles that protect the knee.
exercises.alternative: New to it? Start at 5 minutes and add a minute each session until you reach the full 10.
exercises.stopIf: Any loss of balance or knee pain — slow the belt down or step off onto the side rails.

cooldown: Recumbent bike, 3–4 minutes very easy at Level 1
Seated quad stretch — 30 seconds each leg, gentle pull only, no pain
Seated calf stretch with a towel — 30 seconds each leg
Seated hamstring stretch — 30 seconds each leg, stop at the first gentle pull

weeks.label: Week 4 — Strong finish
weeks.note: Last week of the block. Notice how much stronger your legs feel than a month ago. Tell Shea how each session felt so he can set the next step — maybe a bit more weight on the leg press, maybe a little longer on the backwards walk.
